bounds.termination: first slab exit or electron cutoff

precision_scenes_note: #1013 high-energy low-Z anchors for the FP32-FP64 refinement gate (gate838.py) only; not Geant4-matched benchmark scenes, so the benchmark and the frozen #894 protocol read `scenes` alone. rows_per_history is an estimate until measured

cone.stage: source: photons at creation, unit transmission

precision.protocol: #510 time-to-precision T(eps): warm wall time at which every headline observable of a set meets its target RSE, at each arm's own history count, verified on held-out seeds

headline_floor.note: terminal fractions (and transmitted energy, gated on the transmitted fraction) below fraction_mean, and 4pi photon bands below photons_per_primary in the variance pilot, are diagnostics; the cone yield is always headline (rare by design: its cost is what the comparison measures, bounded by the run budget); bands whose lower edge is at or above the beam energy are excluded

equivalence.frozen: 2026-11-20 (#1041), from pilot evidence only, before held-out seeds 101-103 reported
equivalence.scope_note: owner decision 2026-11-20: no 4pi photon-band set (PyRITE's discrete 4pi path is not optimized) and no discrete-photon PyRITE cone arm; PyRITE arms are pyrite-discrete for the electron transport set and the continuous estimator for the cone
equivalence.test: TOST on the PyRITE/Geant4 ratio of per-primary means, each arm pooled over its held-out seeds at the planned count: pass when the 90% delta-method CI of ln(ratio) lies inside [ln(1-margin), ln(1+margin)]
equivalence.set_rule: intersection-union: a (scene, set, PyRITE arm) is equivalent only if every headline observable of the set passes and both arms met the target RSE on every seed; the conjunction needs no multiplicity adjustment. Only an equivalent set yields a headline T(eps) ratio; other targets and failed gates give qualified outcomes
equivalence.discrepancy_family: two-sided z test of ratio = 1 on ln(ratio), Holm-adjusted at alpha 0.05 across every (scene, set, PyRITE arm, observable) evaluated; flagged cells link to #1039/#1040 or a new discrepancy issue

amendment_v3.frozen: 2026-11-21 (#1041), before held-out seeds 104-106 ran; from held-out seeds 101-103 (jobs 14460, 14462-14464) and the v2 plan only
amendment_v3.reason: v2 sized N at the expected-value count, so 8 of 10 tested sets missed the precision gate at RSE 0.0201-0.0211 on both engines; margins, observables, eps, CI level, set rule and Holm family are unchanged
amendment_v3.plan: precision_plan.py re-planned from the 101-103 held-out evidence (about 50x the pilot histories) with --variance-margin 1.10, --max-run-s 1800, --drop-config geant4-16t, --only-at geant4-1t=0.05, --tail-histories 200000, --protocol-version 3
amendment_v3.floor_rule: a T(eps) row at min_histories measures fixed cost, not throughput: a speedup with either arm at the floor is never headline
amendment_v3.skew_rule: a TOST cell where either arm's pooled |SHIFT/SE| exceeds skew_shift_over_se passes only if the interval recentred by each arm's SHIFT (Cornish-Fisher, #1339) also lies inside the margin
amendment_v3.tail_rule: a cone speedup is headline only if the continuous arm's Hill tail slope, pooled over its runs of >= 50 000 histories in the slice, is at least tail_slope_min (MCNP's finite-variance criterion); otherwise it is qualified as heavy-tailed or insufficient
amendment_v3.fom_rule: FOM = 1/(worst RSE^2 T) per T(eps) row; an arm is FOM-stable when FOM at its largest planned N is within a factor fom_stability_factor of its smallest. The FOM ratio at each arm's largest N is a secondary speed estimate, reported as stable only when both arms are stable, and never a headline

block_note: histories per PyRITE block = min(max_block_histories, block_rows / rows_per_history), split into near-equal blocks (pyrite_bench.scene_block/balanced_blocks). rows_per_history is the mean from job 3039. block_rows is the retained-row memory bound (device staging, then host RAM); larger blocks fill more continuation lanes and shorten each block's sparse tail. Calibration job 3592 (mixed, t32, Q1024): W 1 MeV transport 63/52/40 ns/row at 1250/2500/5000 histories, W 3 MeV 93/75/68 at 2400/4800/9600; light scenes gain nothing past ~20000 histories, and ~80 M rows (pool ~13 GB) spills to host reassembly at 2.3x transport, so 64 M rows keeps margin. Before 2026-11-01 blocks were fixed at about 20 M rows (1250 histories at W 1 MeV).
max_steps_note: per-history step limit (exceeding it raises, never truncates or replays); host_pass sizes Ne*max_steps host row buffers, so block*max_steps <= 5e8. Longest pilot-2805 tracks: Si 300 keV 4213, W 300 keV 9874 rows
